title: Stochastic slot reservation and proactive queue trimming for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Provide predictable per-tenant throughput guarantees while improving burst absorption and minimizing tail latency on Dedicated fleets. Approach: implement a two-part admission control system: 1) stochastic slot reservation - short-lived provisional throughput slots allocated by forecasting near-term demand per-tenant using lightweight Poisson/AR-windowed estimators and a conservative safety margin; 2) proactive queue trimming - early, policy-driven trimming of queued requests based on estimated request cost (token estimate + model-cost multiplier) and business value heuristic (priority tags / customer tier).

Why this is different: rather than coarse fixed reservations or permanent rate caps, the slot reservation adapts quickly and probabilistically to bursts, giving tenants provisional capacity with revocation semantics. Proactive queue trimming reduces expensive tail queues by shedding low-value requests early and preserving headroom for high-value, SLA-bound traffic.

High-level design:
- Slot reservation pool: small epochal window (250ms-2s) where the router issues provisional slot tokens to tenants up to a configurable headroom. Slots have soft TTL and can be revoked if fleet load rises.
- Forecasting engine: per-tenant moving-window request-rate estimator (Poisson smoothing + weighted exponential backoff), emits short-term demand forecast and variance used to size provisional slots.
- Cost estimator: heuristic that combines client-supplied token estimates, model family multiplier, and recent per-token latency to compute an expected resource weight for admission decisions.
- Queue tiers: three logical tiers (urgent, standard, best-effort). Proactive trimming runs periodically on queued best-effort items to drop items below a value threshold when headroom is low.
- Revocation policy: slots revoked using fairness rules: idle-slot reclamation first, then preemptible slots from best-effort flows with notification headers to clients. Revocation includes a soft retry hint for clients (backoff window).
- Fallback: when eviction pressure high, route to cheaper/quantized model variants or degrade max tokens for queued requests if the customer policy allows.

Observable signals and SLOs:
- Admission token issuance rate, revocation rate, and average TTL
- Queue length distribution per tier and per-tenant
- Shed rate and accuracy of cost estimator (predicted vs actual token usage)
- P95/P99 latency for urgent and standard tiers should not regress more than 10% from baseline under typical load
- Fraction of dropped requests should remain below configured per-tenant policy (default 0.5%)

API / Config knobs:
- tenant.reservation.window_ms (250|500|1000|2000)
- tenant.reservation.headroom_pct (0-200)
- tenant.cost_estimator.mode (heuristic|client_provided|ml)
- tenant.queue.tiers (urgent,standard,best-effort) with per-tier weight and drop_threshold
- fleet.revoke_order (idle_first|weighted_fair)

Rollout plan:
1) Simulation stage: build a synthetic traffic generator (mix of steady, bursty, and expensive requests) and validate fairness and SLOs offline.
2) Canary in dedicated test pool: enable for internal test tenants with conservative headroom. Collect metrics and tune thresholds.
3) Gradual rollout by tenant size: start with small tenants, then medium, then large. Include an automatic rollback trigger when shed rate exceeds X or latency regressions exceed thresholds.

Backward compatibility: default behavior is off for existing dedicated tenants; new dedicated presets may default to conservative slots. SDK changes limited to optional hints (estimated_tokens, priority_hint) to improve cost estimator accuracy.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulation shows <=5% additional token cost for same effective throughput and <10% p99 latency regression on urgent tier under mixed load.
- Live canary for 3 internal tenants for 72h with metrics meeting SLOs.
- Unit and integration tests covering slot lifecycle, revocation, and trimming logic.

implementation_notes: Start by landing forecasting and slot-pool primitives behind feature flag. Keep eviction decisions centralized in the routing tier to simplify invariants. Avoid global locks; use per-shard pools. Use estimators with cheap ops to keep router CPU overhead <2%.
risks: Estimator underprediction could cause unexpected shedding of high-value traffic
Telemetry gaps might make tuning thresholds difficult
Complexity of revocation semantics could increase client-side retries and error churn
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for slot lifecycle and revocation; 2) Integration tests simulating tenant mixes; 3) Chaos tests that force sudden fleet overload to validate graceful fallback and rollbacks; 4) Canary monitoring with automated rollback on SLO violation
